frozen.$why: Fifty-three commits to this file in twenty-four days and twenty-two reversals. Every one was individually defensible and the week never landed. The gate makes "an agent redesigns the week" unrepresentable until the review date. To change the week before then, add {on, hisWords, hash} to `changes` with his quoted sentence of at least eight words and the new hash from --print-hash. The commit message should carry the same words.

$time.how: minutes = 10 + 2.7 x sets, from his watch: 21 to 25 sets took 57 to 94 minutes (2026-09-28 to 10-11), and his first Pizarro session was about 26 sets in about 70 minutes (2026-11-18, his words). The slow 2026-08 sessions are left out.

blocks.label: Lead lift, leg raises in the rest
blocks.why: First, while the one rack is free: heels raised, as deep as your back stays flat. Two or three lighter sets build up to the working weight, and that is the warm-up. And the leg raises ride in its rest on the bar above the rack.

exercises.name: BB Back Squat
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Heels on two small plates (or a wedge), feet a little wider than hips, toes slightly out. Breathe in and hold it, brace your stomach, then sit down between your feet as deep as you can keep your back flat. Knees push out over your second toe. Fresh breath every rep. Deeper, not heavier, is the first progress. Stop when a rep looks different.

alts.name: Hack Squat
alts.cue: Back flat on the pad, feet shoulder width in the middle of the platform. Go as deep as your back stays on the pad, then press. Use this if the one rack is taken.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Lighter than the back squat. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Fingertips just hook under the bar; the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. Because the bar is in front, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier. If the elbows drop the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Hang from the bar, hands shoulder width, shoulders pulled down away from your ears. Brace your stomach, then lift your legs nearly straight until your feet reach hip height, curling your hips up at the top. Lower over two seconds without swinging. When ten clean reps are easy, lift higher.

alts.name: Plank w/ Shoulder Taps
alts.cue: On the floor. High plank on your hands, feet wide apart for balance. Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, put it back, tap with the other. Success looks like: your hips do not rock side to side as the hand leaves the floor. If they rock, put your feet wider. 3x10 each side.

alts.name: Band Pallof Press
alts.cue: Band anchored at chest height on a rack post, stand sideways, both hands on the band at your chest. Press straight out and resist the twist, hold 2 seconds. Only if every cable column is taken: there is no way to record which band you used, so the number cannot move.

alts.name: Hollow Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

exercises.whyHere: the leg raises ride in its rest on the bar above the rack

blocks.label: More quads, lateral raise in the rest
blocks.why: More work for the fronts of the thighs after the squat, on a machine that needs no balance. And the lateral raise rides in its rest, with a pair of dumbbells carried to the machine.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Feet shoulder width in the middle of the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back lifting off the pad, then press without locking your knees hard.

alts.name: Hack Squat
alts.cue: Back flat on the pad, feet shoulder width. As deep as your back stays on the pad, then press.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if pouring from two jugs. Lower about twice as slowly as you lifted. Success: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top. If either fails, go lighter.

alts.name: KB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

exercises.whyHere: the lateral raise rides in its rest, with a pair of dumbbells carried to the machine

blocks.label: Back of the thigh, Cossack in the rest
blocks.why: The hamstrings directly, on the machine. Take the seated one if there are both. And the Cossack squat rides in its rest, one dumbbell carried to the machine: hip range and the inner thighs.

exercises.name: Leg Curl Machine
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Seated or lying, whichever the gym has. Line your knee up with the round pivot on the side of the machine, the pad just above your heels. Curl your heels toward your bum, hold one second, then let it back over three seconds until your legs are nearly straight. Hips stay down on the seat. First time: pick a weight you could lift 15 times and stop at 10.

alts.name: Stability Ball Hamstring Curl
alts.cue: On the floor, heels on a ball, hips up. Roll the ball in toward your bum by bending the knees, keep the hips up, roll it out slowly. 3x10.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Feet very wide, toes slightly out, a dumbbell held at your chest. Sit down over ONE leg until that thigh is deep, the other leg straight with its toes pointing up. Heel of the bent leg stays down. Stand back up through the middle and go to the other side. Start with no weight or a light dumbbell; depth first.

alts.name: DB Lateral Lunge
alts.cue: Step wide to one side, sit back over that leg with the other straight, push back to standing. Less depth than the Cossack.

exercises.whyHere: the Cossack squat rides in its rest, one dumbbell carried to the machine

blocks.label: Sideways, curl in the rest
blocks.why: The glute muscles that move the leg out to the side, which a squat barely touches. And the curl rides in its rest, with a pair of dumbbells carried to the machine.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction Machine
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. The machine where you sit with pads on the OUTSIDE of your knees and push your legs apart. Sit tall, hands on the handles, push out wide, hold one second, then let the legs come back slowly without the weights touching. Leaning a little forward puts more of it into the side of your bum.

alts.name: Cable Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Ankle strap on the low pulley, stand side-on and sweep the far leg out to the side and back slowly. 12 a side.

alts.name: Banded Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Band above the knees, sitting on the end of a bench, push the knees apart and back slowly. 20.

exercises.name: DB Biceps Curl
exercises.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, elbows still at your sides, no swinging. Curl up, squeeze at the top, lower slowly all the way.

alts.name: DB Hammer Curl
alts.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs the whole way, like holding two hammers. Curl both up together until the dumbbells reach shoulder height, elbows staying at your sides, then lower slowly. Your torso does not rock. If your elbows drift forward or your back leans, go lighter.

alts.name: Incline DB Curl
alts.cue: A dumbbell in each hand on the incline bench. Sit with the backs of your upper arms flat on the slanted pad and keep them there. Curl up until your forearms are vertical, squeeze, then lower ALL THE WAY until the arms are straight. The pad is the point: it makes swinging impossible, so the weight will feel heavier than a standing curl. Start lighter than you think.

exercises.whyHere: the curl rides in its rest, with a pair of dumbbells carried to the machine

blocks.label: Front of the thigh, carry in the rest
blocks.why: The quads alone, a short finish on the same row of machines. And the farmer carry rides in its rest, heavy and last, so your grip is still free for every lift before it.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Knees lined up with the machine's pivot, pad just above the ankles. Straighten your legs fully and hold one second, then lower slowly.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Heaviest dumbbells you can hold for the time. Grip the handle dead in the middle so the dumbbell hangs level, squeeze hard, shoulders down, arms tight against your sides, and take short quick steps: long steps start the swing. Walk tall. When the time is easy, take the next dumbbell up.

alts.name: DB Static Hold
alts.cue: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: KB Farmer Carry
alts.cue: Kettlebells instead, if the gym has them. Use this one when the dumbbells are taken, not when you want it heavier. They hang differently and swing a little, so the grip works harder at the same weight.

alts.name: KB Suitcase Hold
alts.cue: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.

exercises.whyHere: the farmer carry rides in its rest, heavy and last, so your grip is still free for every lift before it

$time.how: minutes = 10 + 2.7 x sets, from his watch: 21 to 25 sets took 57 to 94 minutes (2026-09-28 to 10-11), and his first Pizarro session was about 26 sets in about 70 minutes (2026-11-18, his words). The slow 2026-08 sessions are left out.

blocks.label: Lead lift
blocks.why: Chest first, because the lift done first gains the most strength. The marker: from 27 kg dumbbells for 9 to the 32 kg pair for 8. Two or three lighter sets build up to the working weight, and that is the warm-up.

exercises.name: DB Incline Press
exercises.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat. Shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower until you feel a stretch across the chest, pause one second, press up over your lower chest. Success: a stretch across the chest at the bottom, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder.

alts.name: BB Bench Press
alts.cue: Flat bench inside the rack. Set the safety pins at chest height BEFORE you load the bar, every time, because you train alone. Feet flat, grip a little wider than your shoulders, shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower to your lower chest until it touches lightly, press up, same spot every rep. If you have to bounce it, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Machine Chest Press
alts.cue: A press on a machine, moderate rather than heavy: the barbell bench is where the press gets pushed. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

blocks.label: Shoulders
blocks.why: The sides of the shoulders, with the dumbbells you are already standing at.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if pouring from two jugs. Lower about twice as slowly as you lifted. Success: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top. If either fails, go lighter.

alts.name: KB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

blocks.label: Triceps
blocks.why: The backs of the arms, the push at the end of every swim stroke.

exercises.name: DB Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.cue: Sit on the end of the bench, back tall, one dumbbell held in both hands above your head, arms straight. Bend only at the elbows to lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch in the back of your arms, elbows pointing up and staying close. Straighten back up. Upper arms stay still the whole set.

blocks.label: Biceps
blocks.why: The fronts of the arms, still at the dumbbell rack before you move.

exercises.name: DB Biceps Curl
exercises.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, elbows still at your sides, no swinging. Curl up, squeeze at the top, lower slowly all the way.

alts.name: DB Hammer Curl
alts.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs the whole way, like holding two hammers. Curl both up together until the dumbbells reach shoulder height, elbows staying at your sides, then lower slowly. Your torso does not rock. If your elbows drift forward or your back leans, go lighter.

alts.name: Incline DB Curl
alts.cue: A dumbbell in each hand on the incline bench. Sit with the backs of your upper arms flat on the slanted pad and keep them there. Curl up until your forearms are vertical, squeeze, then lower ALL THE WAY until the arms are straight. The pad is the point: it makes swinging impossible, so the weight will feel heavier than a standing curl. Start lighter than you think.

blocks.label: More chest
blocks.why: A second chest exercise, on the machine, to bring chest to twelve sets a week.

exercises.name: Pec Fly Machine
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Seat so the handles are at chest height. Elbows slightly bent and fixed. Bring the handles together in front of your chest, squeeze one second, open slowly until you feel the stretch across the chest.

alts.name: Cable Fly
alts.cue: Handles at shoulder height, step forward, bring your hands together in front of your chest with the elbows slightly bent. Open slowly.

blocks.label: Row
blocks.why: The back, on the plate-loaded high row you used on your first day. Log one side.

exercises.name: High Row (plate-loaded, kg a side)
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Log the plates on ONE side, as you wrote it. Chest on the pad, pull the handles down and back toward your ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades together for one second, let the arms go all the way straight.

alts.name: Incline Low Row (plate-loaded, kg a side)
alts.cue: Chest on the pad, pull the handles to your stomach, squeeze, arms straight at the bottom. Log one side.

alts.name: Seated Cable Row
alts.cue: Sit tall, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze the shoulder blades, arms straight on the way back.

blocks.label: Lats
blocks.why: The pull of your swim stroke: the lats, from a full stretch at the top.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight.

alts.name: Assisted Pull-Up
alts.cue: Counterweight set for 8 clean reps. Log the counterweight; it should go DOWN over time.

blocks.label: Posture
blocks.why: The backs of the shoulders that hold your posture, light and slow.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Rope on the cable column at forehead height. Hold the rope ends with thumbs toward you, step back until the arms are straight. Pull the rope to your face, splitting the ends past your ears, elbows high and wide, and squeeze the shoulder blades together for one second. Back slowly. Light: if your lower back leans back, it is too heavy.

alts.name: DB Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, chest forward to about 45 degrees, back flat. Open your arms out to the sides until your hands are level with your shoulders, squeeze, lower slowly. Light.

alts.name: Cable Reverse Fly
alts.cue: At the cable column, a handle in each hand, arms crossed in front. Open the arms out to the sides until the hands are level with the shoulders, squeeze, back slowly. Light.

$time.how: minutes = 10 + 2.7 x sets, from his watch: 21 to 25 sets took 57 to 94 minutes (2026-09-28 to 10-11), and his first Pizarro session was about 26 sets in about 70 minutes (2026-11-18, his words). The slow 2026-08 sessions are left out.

blocks.label: Lead lift
blocks.why: The hinge first, fresh, for the hamstrings and glutes. Two or three lighter sets build up to the working weight, and that is the warm-up.

exercises.name: BB Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: The heavy hinge. Breathe IN and tighten your stomach. Bar touches your legs the whole way, shins vertical. Bend the knees slightly and FREEZE them, then push your hips back toward the wall behind you. Go down until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height, and no further. Squeeze your bum and drive the hips forward to stand. If your lower back rounds you went too far. Straps are fine.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.

alts.name: KB Swing
alts.cue: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 16 kg. 2x12.

alts.name: Smith RDL
alts.cue: Bar on rails so it cannot drift away from your legs. Useful for grooving the hinge when you are tired.

alts.name: B-Stance RDL
alts.cue: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.

alts.name: Single-Leg RDL
alts.cue: One dumbbell, in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg. Stand on one leg with a soft knee, push the hips back and let the free leg travel straight back behind you as the dumbbell lowers down the standing shin. Stop when the hamstring of the standing leg pulls; do not chase the floor. Success: your hips stay level, no rolling open to the side. Hold the rack with your free hand if you wobble, that is not cheating. 8/leg.

blocks.label: Glutes, heavy
blocks.why: The glutes alone. Squats and hip thrusts built about the same glute in a head-to-head study, so the week has both.

exercises.name: Smith Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Bar low on the rails, a pad on your hip crease, upper back on a bench, feet flat about one and a half shoulder widths apart. Drive your hips up until your shins are vertical and your thighs level with the floor, no higher: ribs stay down. One second up, two seconds down, hips brush the floor between reps.

alts.name: Hip Thrust Machine
alts.cue: If the gym has one, use it instead of the Smith: back on the pad, belt or pad across the hip crease, feet flat. Drive the hips up until your thighs are level, ribs down, one second up and two down. First time: start light and work up until 10 feels hard.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

firstWeight.say: First try: start with a weight you could lift 15 times, then work up until 10 reps feels hard, about 2 left in the tank. Log that weight.

blocks.label: Glutes, lighter
blocks.why: More glute work on the back extension: round the upper back slightly and drive up with your hips.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Pad just below your hip bones. Round your upper back slightly and squeeze your glutes to come up until your body is straight, not past it. Hold a plate at your chest when 14 is easy.

blocks.label: Sideways
blocks.why: The glute muscles that move the leg out to the side, which a hinge barely touches.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction Machine
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. The machine where you sit with pads on the OUTSIDE of your knees and push your legs apart. Sit tall, hands on the handles, push out wide, hold one second, then let the legs come back slowly without the weights touching. Leaning a little forward puts more of it into the side of your bum.

alts.name: Cable Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Ankle strap on the low pulley, stand side-on and sweep the far leg out to the side and back slowly. 12 a side.

alts.name: Banded Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Band above the knees, sitting on the end of a bench, push the knees apart and back slowly. 20.

blocks.label: Trunk
blocks.why: The stomach muscles resisting a twist, at the cable column, before the single-leg work.

exercises.name: Cable Pallof Press
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Cable at chest height, stand side-on, both hands on the handle at your chest. Press straight out and hold 2 seconds without letting it twist you, bring it back. Both sides.

blocks.label: One leg at a time
blocks.why: One leg at a time, where you feel the glutes most. Lean slightly forward.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Back foot laces-down on the bench, front foot far enough forward that you can sink straight down. Dumbbells at your sides. Lean your chest slightly forward to put it in the glute, lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor, push up through the front heel.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Step straight back, back knee toward the floor, push up through the front heel.

blocks.label: Step-up
blocks.why: Your step-ups, kept in the week on your words: one leg driving you up onto the bench.

exercises.name: DB Step-Up
exercises.cue: Box or bench at knee height, a dumbbell in each hand. Put your whole foot on top and drive up through that HEEL until you stand tall on it. The foot on the floor does not push off: lift it like a passenger. Lower slowly on the same leg. All reps on one leg, then the other. Success: your knee tracks over your toes and the top hip does not drop.

firstWeight.say: First try: start with 14 kg dumbbells and work up until 8 a leg feels hard, about 2 left in the tank. Log that weight.

alts.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

blocks.label: Carry
blocks.why: A carry with one dumbbell: the side of your trunk works to keep you upright.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. One heavy dumbbell in one hand, walk tall without leaning toward it, 20 seconds a side. The free side of your body does the work.

$time.how: minutes = 10 + 2.7 x sets, from his watch: 21 to 25 sets took 57 to 94 minutes (2026-09-28 to 10-11), and his first Pizarro session was about 26 sets in about 70 minutes (2026-11-18, his words). The slow 2026-08 sessions are left out.

blocks.label: Lead lift
blocks.why: Chest first again, on the machine, where the shoulder is held steady. Two or three lighter sets build up to the working weight, and that is the warm-up.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.cue: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest. Back flat on the pad, feet flat. Press the handles forward until your arms are straight but not locked, then let them come back under control until you feel the stretch across your chest. Shoulders stay down and back against the pad the whole set.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat. Shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower until you feel a stretch across the chest, pause one second, press up over your lower chest. Success: a stretch across the chest at the bottom, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder.

blocks.label: Vertical pull
blocks.why: The pull-up machine: the lats, the main engine of your swim stroke.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 5 kg of assistance off.

alts.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
alts.cue: Loop a band over the bar on top of the rack, pull one end through the other, and put one knee in the loop. Hands a little wider than your shoulders. Pull your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin is over the bar, then lower slowly to straight arms. Same band every time; when 10 is easy, use a lighter band.

alts.name: Lat Pulldown
alts.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight.

blocks.label: Posture, hammer curl in the rest
blocks.why: The backs of the shoulders, on the same machine as the pec fly turned round. And the hammer curl rides in its rest, with a pair of dumbbells carried to the machine.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Machine
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Sit facing the pad of the pec fly machine, handles in front at shoulder height. Open your arms out to the sides until the hands are level with your shoulders, squeeze one second, back slowly. Light.

alts.name: Cable Reverse Fly
alts.cue: A handle in each hand, arms crossed in front, open out to the sides, squeeze, back slowly. Light.

exercises.name: DB Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Palms facing each other, elbows at your sides, curl up without swinging, lower slowly.
exercises.whyHere: the hammer curl rides in its rest, with a pair of dumbbells carried to the machine

blocks.label: Row
blocks.why: A row one arm at a time, with the dumbbells, for the middle of the back.

exercises.name: DB Single-Arm Row
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Same bench as the press, set flat for this. One knee and the same-side hand on the bench, the other foot on the floor, back flat. Dumbbell hanging straight down. Pull it to your hip by driving the ELBOW back past your ribs, pause, lower all the way until the shoulder stretches. All reps on one arm, then the other. Your back does not twist to lift it.

firstWeight.say: First try: start with a 22 kg dumbbell and work up until 8 an arm feels hard, about 2 left in the tank. Log that weight.

alts.name: BB Row
alts.cue: Hinge forward until your chest is roughly parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent, back flat. Breathe in and brace. Pull the bar to your belly button by driving your ELBOWS back past your ribs, then lower it all the way under control. Same bar as the bench: change the plates, not the rack. If you have to stand up to move the bar, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Seated Cable Row
alts.cue: Tall chest, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze the shoulder blades, let it stretch all the way forward.

alts.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
alts.cue: Same bench as the press, one notch steeper, lying face down with your chest on the pad and a dumbbell in each hand. Pull your elbows back past your ribs and squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower until the arms are straight. The bench holds your back still, so nothing can cheat.

blocks.label: Shoulders
blocks.why: The sides of the shoulders on the cable, which keeps the pull on all the way up.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Cable at its lowest, stand side-on, handle in the far hand. Raise the arm out to the side to shoulder height, slightly in front of you, lower slowly. Both sides.

alts.name: DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Dumbbells at your sides, raise out to shoulder height, lower slowly.

blocks.label: Triceps
blocks.why: The backs of the arms at the cable, the push at the end of a swim stroke.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Rope or bar at the top of the cable. Elbows pinned to your sides, push down until your arms are straight, squeeze, back up slowly only to where the elbows stay still.

blocks.label: Abs
blocks.why: At the bar, last: the stomach muscles, legs lifted straight without swinging.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Hang from the bar, hands shoulder width, shoulders pulled down away from your ears. Brace your stomach, then lift your legs nearly straight until your feet reach hip height, curling your hips up at the top. Lower over two seconds without swinging. When ten clean reps are easy, lift higher.

alts.name: Plank w/ Shoulder Taps
alts.cue: On the floor. High plank on your hands, feet wide apart for balance. Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, put it back, tap with the other. Success looks like: your hips do not rock side to side as the hand leaves the floor. If they rock, put your feet wider. 3x10 each side.

alts.name: Band Pallof Press
alts.cue: Band anchored at chest height on a rack post, stand sideways, both hands on the band at your chest. Press straight out and resist the twist, hold 2 seconds. Only if every cable column is taken: there is no way to record which band you used, so the number cannot move.

alts.name: Hollow Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

$time.how: minutes = 10 + 2.7 x sets, from his watch: 21 to 25 sets took 57 to 94 minutes (2026-09-28 to 10-11), and his first Pizarro session was about 26 sets in about 70 minutes (2026-11-18, his words). The slow 2026-08 sessions are left out.

blocks.label: Lead lift
blocks.why: Depth first: heels raised, a pause at the bottom. Full squats grew the glutes about three times as much as half squats in one study. Two or three lighter sets build up to the working weight, and that is the warm-up.

exercises.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Heels on small plates, a dumbbell held upright at your chest. Sit straight down between your feet as deep as you can with a flat back, pause one second at the bottom, stand. Depth is the point of this one.

blocks.label: Hinge on one leg
blocks.why: Your single-leg RDL, kept on your words: balance and the hamstrings, one side at a time.

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL
exercises.cue: One dumbbell, in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg, the other hand on a bench or rack. Soft standing knee, push the hips back and let the free leg travel straight back as the dumbbell lowers down the standing shin. Stop when that hamstring pulls; do not chase the floor. Hips stay level. Holding on is the point: your hamstring decides the weight, not your balance.

alts.name: DB RDL
alts.cue: Both feet down, a dumbbell in each hand: the same hinge without the balance. Use it on a day one leg feels off.

blocks.label: Hips
blocks.why: The deep side-to-side squat again, for hip range and the inner thighs.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Feet very wide, toes slightly out, a dumbbell held at your chest. Sit down over ONE leg until that thigh is deep, the other leg straight with its toes pointing up. Heel of the bent leg stays down. Stand back up through the middle and go to the other side. Start with no weight or a light dumbbell; depth first.

alts.name: DB Lateral Lunge
alts.cue: Step wide to one side, sit back over that leg with the other straight, push back to standing. Less depth than the Cossack.

blocks.label: Chest
blocks.why: A third chest session, short, with the dumbbells before you leave the rack.

exercises.name: DB Incline Press
exercises.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat. Shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower until you feel a stretch across the chest, pause one second, press up over your lower chest. Success: a stretch across the chest at the bottom, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder.

alts.name: BB Bench Press
alts.cue: Flat bench inside the rack. Set the safety pins at chest height BEFORE you load the bar, every time, because you train alone. Feet flat, grip a little wider than your shoulders, shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower to your lower chest until it touches lightly, press up, same spot every rep. If you have to bounce it, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Machine Chest Press
alts.cue: A press on a machine, moderate rather than heavy: the barbell bench is where the press gets pushed. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

blocks.label: Grip and carry
blocks.why: Heavy, before the machines, so the last lifts do not need your grip.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Heaviest dumbbells you can hold for the time. Grip the handle dead in the middle so the dumbbell hangs level, squeeze hard, shoulders down, arms tight against your sides, and take short quick steps: long steps start the swing. Walk tall. When the time is easy, take the next dumbbell up.

alts.name: DB Static Hold
alts.cue: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: KB Farmer Carry
alts.cue: Kettlebells instead, if the gym has them. Use this one when the dumbbells are taken, not when you want it heavier. They hang differently and swing a little, so the grip works harder at the same weight.

alts.name: KB Suitcase Hold
alts.cue: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.

blocks.label: Glutes
blocks.why: The glutes alone, heavy: the second hip thrust of the week, on the Smith machine or a loaded bar on the bench.

exercises.name: Smith Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Bar low on the rails, a pad on your hip crease, upper back on a bench, feet flat about one and a half shoulder widths apart. Drive your hips up until your shins are vertical and your thighs level with the floor, no higher: ribs stay down. One second up, two seconds down, hips brush the floor between reps.

alts.name: Hip Thrust Machine
alts.cue: If the gym has one, use it instead of the Smith: back on the pad, belt or pad across the hip crease, feet flat. Drive the hips up until your thighs are level, ribs down, one second up and two down. First time: start light and work up until 10 feels hard.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

firstWeight.say: First try: start with a weight you could lift 15 times, then work up until 10 reps feels hard, about 2 left in the tank. Log that weight.

blocks.label: Back of the thigh
blocks.why: The hamstrings directly, on the machine.

exercises.name: Leg Curl Machine
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Seated or lying, whichever the gym has. Line your knee up with the round pivot on the side of the machine, the pad just above your heels. Curl your heels toward your bum, hold one second, then let it back over three seconds until your legs are nearly straight. Hips stay down on the seat. First time: pick a weight you could lift 15 times and stop at 10.

alts.name: Stability Ball Hamstring Curl
alts.cue: On the floor, heels on a ball, hips up. Roll the ball in toward your bum by bending the knees, keep the hips up, roll it out slowly. 3x10.

blocks.label: Posture
blocks.why: The backs of the shoulders that hold your posture, light and slow.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Rope on the cable column at forehead height. Hold the rope ends with thumbs toward you, step back until the arms are straight. Pull the rope to your face, splitting the ends past your ears, elbows high and wide, and squeeze the shoulder blades together for one second. Back slowly. Light: if your lower back leans back, it is too heavy.

alts.name: DB Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, chest forward to about 45 degrees, back flat. Open your arms out to the sides until your hands are level with your shoulders, squeeze, lower slowly. Light.

alts.name: Cable Reverse Fly
alts.cue: At the cable column, a handle in each hand, arms crossed in front. Open the arms out to the sides until the hands are level with the shoulders, squeeze, back slowly. Light.
